content.text: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.
When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

You have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

If you use an object—such as a table leg, frying pan, or bottle—as a makeshift weapon, see "[Improvised Weapons](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/improvised-weapons)" in the rules glossary. Also see those rules if you wield a weapon in an unusual way, such as using a Ranged weapon to make a melee attack.

When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a [Shortsword](srd-5.2/06/weapons/shortsword) in one hand and a [Dagger](srd-5.2/06/weapons/dagger) in the other using the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.
You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the [Ammunition](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/ammunition) or [Thrown](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/thrown) property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.
A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks) with it.

If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.
A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.
A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

When you make the extra attack of the [Light](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/light) property, you can make it as part of the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition.

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
Each weapon has a mastery property, which is usable only by a character who has a feature, such as Weapon Mastery, that unlocks the property for the character. The properties are defined below.

content.text: When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d6 Acid damage.

When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist's Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 1d4 Fire damage and start [burning](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/burning).

As a Bonus Action, you can drink a vial of Antitoxin to gain [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws to avoid or end the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 hour.

An Arcane Focus takes one of the forms in the Arcane Focuses table and is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic. A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard can use such an item as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus).
A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can spill Ball Bearings from their pouch. They spread to cover a level, 10-foot-square area within 10 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or have the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Ball Bearings.
A Barrel holds up to 40 gallons of liquid or up to 4 cubic feet of dry goods.
A Basket holds up to 40 pounds within 2 cubic feet.
A Bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. While in a Bedroll, you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold (see the *System Reference Document*).
When rung as a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, a Bell produces a sound that can be heard up to 60 feet away.
While wrapped in a blanket, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against extreme cold (see the *System Reference Document*).
A Block and Tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

A Book contains fiction or nonfiction. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana), [History](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/history), [Nature](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/nature), or [Religion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/religion)) checks you make about that topic.
A Glass Bottle holds up to 1½ pints.
A Bucket holds up to half a cubic foot of contents.

A Burglar's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Ball Bearings](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ball-bearings), [Bell](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/bell), 10 [Candles](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/candle), [Crowbar](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/crowbar), [Hooded Lantern](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lantern-hooded), 7 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 5 days of [Rations](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rations), [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope), [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox), and [Waterskin](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/waterskin).

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can spread Caltrops from their bag to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Caltrops.
For 1 hour, a lit Candle sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 5-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 5 feet.
A Crossbow Bolt Case holds up to 20 [Bolts](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ammunition).
A Map or Scroll Case holds up to 10 sheets of [paper](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/paper) or 5 sheets of [parchment](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/parchment).

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can wrap a Chain around an unwilling creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the [Grappled](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/grappled), [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated), or [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Chain requires the creature to make a successful DC 18 Dexterity ([Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics)) check as an action. Bursting the Chain requires a successful DC 20 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check as an action.
A Chest holds up to 12 cubic feet of contents.

A Climber's Kit includes boot tips, gloves, pitons, and a harness. As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can use the Climber's Kit to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the anchor point, and you can't move more than 25 feet from there without undoing the anchor as a Bonus Action.
Fine Clothes are made of expensive fabrics and adorned with expertly crafted details. Some events and locations admit only people wearing these clothes.
Traveler's Clothes are resilient garments designed for travel in various environments.
A Component Pouch is watertight and filled with compartments that hold all the free Material components of your spells.
While wearing a Costume, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on any ability check you make to impersonate the person or type of person it represents.
Using a Crowbar gives you [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Strength checks where the Crowbar's leverage can be applied.

A Diplomat's Pack contains the following items: [Chest](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/chest), [Fine Clothes](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/clothes-fine), [Ink](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ink), 5 [Ink Pens](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ink-pen), [Lamp](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lamp), 2 [Map or Scroll Cases](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/case-map-or-scroll), 4 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 5 sheets of [Paper](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/paper), 5 sheets of [Parchment](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/parchment), [Perfume](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/perfume), and [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox).

A Druidic Focus takes one of the forms in the Druidic Focuses table and is carved, tied with ribbon, or painted to channel primal magic. A Druid or Ranger can use such an object as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus).

A Dungeoneer's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Caltrops](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/caltrops), [Crowbar](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/crowbar), 2 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 10 days of [Rations](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rations), [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope), [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox), 10 [Torches](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/torch), and [Waterskin](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/waterskin).

An Entertainer's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Bedroll](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/bedroll), [Bell](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/bell), [Bullseye Lantern](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lantern-bullseye), 3 [Costumes](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/costume), [Mirror](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/mirror), 8 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 9 days of [Rations](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rations), [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox), and [Waterskin](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/waterskin).

An Explorer's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Bedroll](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/bedroll), 2 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 10 days of [Rations](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rations), [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope), [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox), 10 [Torches](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/torch), and [Waterskin](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/waterskin).
A Flask holds up to 1 pint.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can throw the Grappling Hook at a railing, a ledge, or another catch within 50 feet of yourself, and the hook catches on if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity ([Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics)) check. If you tied a [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope) to the hook, you can then climb it.

A Healer's Kit has ten uses. As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an [Unconscious](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/unconscious) creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom ([Medicine](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/medicine)) check.

A Holy Symbol takes one of the forms in the Holy Symbol table and is bejeweled or painted to channel divine magic. A Cleric or Paladin can use a Holy Symbol as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus).
The table indicates whether a Holy Symbol needs to be held, worn, or borne on fabric (such as a tabard or banner) or a Shield.

When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Holy Water. Target one creature you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 Radiant damage if it is a Fiend or an Undead.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature.
Ink comes in a 1-ounce bottle, which provides enough ink to write about 500 pages.
Using [Ink](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ink), an Ink Pen is used to write or draw.
A Jug holds up to 1 gallon.
A Ladder is 10 feet tall. You must climb to move up or down it.

A Lamp burns [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil) as fuel to cast [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 15-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet.

A Bullseye Lantern burns [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil) as fuel to cast [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 60-foot [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone) and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 60 feet.

A Hooded Lantern burns [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil) as fuel to cast [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 30-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, or raise it again.

A Lock comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use [Thieves' Tools](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/thieves-tools) to pick this Lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check.

A Magnifying Glass grants [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on any ability check made to appraise or inspect a highly detailed item. Lighting a fire with a Magnifying Glass requires light as bright as sunlight to focus, tinder to ignite, and about 5 minutes for the fire to ignite.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the [Grappled](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/grappled), [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated), or [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check. While bound, a creature has [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls, and the creature is [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) if the Manacles are attached to a chain or hook that is fixed in place. Escaping the Manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check as an action. Bursting them requires a successful DC 25 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check as an action.

Each set of Manacles comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use [Thieves' Tools](srd-5.2/06/tools/other-tools/thieves-tools) to pick the Manacles' lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check.

If you consult an accurate Map, you gain a +5 bonus to Wisdom ([Survival](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/survival)) checks you make to find your way in the place represented on it.
A handheld steel Mirror is useful for personal cosmetics but also for peeking around corners and reflecting light as a signal.

When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a Net. Target a creature you can see within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or have the [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition until it escapes. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 10 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. Destroying the Net (AC 10; 5 HP; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage) also frees the target, ending the effect.
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

content.label: Dousing a Creature or an Object
content.text: When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra 5 Fire damage from burning oil.

content.label: Dousing a Space
content.text: You can take the [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

content.label: Fuel
content.text: Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn't need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.
One sheet of Paper can hold about 250 handwritten words.
One sheet of Parchment can hold about 250 handwritten words.

Perfume comes in a 4-ounce vial. For 1 hour after applying Perfume to yourself, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Charisma ([Persuasion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/persuasion)) checks made to influence an [Indifferent](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/indifferent) Humanoid within 5 feet of yourself.

As a Bonus Action, you can use a vial of Basic Poison to coat one weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. A creature that takes Piercing or Slashing damage from the poisoned weapon or ammunition takes an extra 1d4 Poison damage. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute or until its damage is dealt, whichever comes first.

A Pole is 10 feet long. You can use it to touch something up to 10 feet away. If you must make a Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check as part of a [High](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/high-jump) or [Long Jump](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-jump), you can use the Pole to vault, giving yourself [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the check.
An Iron Pot holds up to 1 gallon.
A Pouch holds up to 6 pounds within one-fifth of a cubic foot.

A Priest's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Blanket](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/blanket), [Holy Water](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/holy-water), [Lamp](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lamp), 7 days of [Rations](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rations), [Robe](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/robe), and [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox).
A Quiver holds up to 20 [Arrows](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ammunition).

You can use a Portable Ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus to the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on this check.

Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See "[Malnutrition](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/malnutrition)" in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.
A Robe has vocational or ceremonial significance. Some events and locations admit only people wearing a Robe bearing certain colors or symbols.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the [Grappled](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/grappled), [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated), or [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity ([Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics)) check as an action.
A Sack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot.

A Scholar's Pack contains the following items: [Backpack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/backpack), [Book](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/book), [Ink](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ink), [Ink Pen](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ink-pen), [Lamp](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lamp), 10 flasks of [Oil](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/oil), 10 sheets of [Parchment](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/parchment), and [Tinderbox](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/tinderbox).
Working for 1 hour, you can use a Shovel to dig a hole that is 5 feet on each side in soil or similar material.
When blown as a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, a Signal Whistle produces a sound that can be heard up to 600 feet away.

Iron Spikes come in bundles of ten. As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can use a blunt object, such as a [Light Hammer](srd-5.2/06/weapons/light-hammer), to hammer a spike into wood, earth, or a similar material. You can do so to jam a door shut or to then tie a [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope) or [Chain](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/chain) to the Spike.
Objects viewed through a Spyglass are magnified to twice their size.
String is 10 feet long. You can tie a knot in it as a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action.
A Tent sleeps up to two Small or Medium creatures.

A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a [Candle](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/candle), [Lamp](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lamp), Lantern, or [Torch](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/torch)—or anything else with exposed fuel—takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 20-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 20 feet. When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.
A Vial holds up to 4 ounces.
A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk [dehydration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dehydration).

Ammunition is required by a weapon that has the [Ammunition](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/ammunition) property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.
A saddle comes with a bit, a bridle, reins, and any other equipment needed to use the saddle. An Exotic Saddle is required for riding an aquatic or a flying mount.

A saddle comes with a bit, a bridle, reins, and any other equipment needed to use the saddle. A Military Saddle gives [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on any ability check you make to remain mounted.
A saddle comes with a bit, a bridle, reins, and any other equipment needed to use the saddle.
